Independent bounded beta Gram calculation through N=8
correctness.rationale: The pullback of the j-th block monomial has external character u^B v^(i+C) w^C, so distinct triples are orthogonal even with the multiplier weight |a|². Factoring (z−1)^i(z+1)^δ z^m leaves powers t^(m−j), where t=(2+z+z^(−1))/4; the normalized circular measure pushes to the arcsine density. This gives the stated beta weight and compressed multiplication by 1−t. Its characteristic polynomial is the degree-(m+1) orthogonal polynomial after the linear change of variable ζ=1−2t, which gives the stated Jacobi parameters and accounts for the whole multiset. On the larger space of all circle polynomials of degree at most N the squared multiplier form is the (N+1)-path tridiagonal with diagonal 1/2 and off-diagonal −1/4, giving the lower bound and a unique sine-coefficient minimizer. That polynomial has degree N, is nonzero at +1, and has order zero at −1 for even N and order one for odd N, from its finite sine-sum generating identity. Its reciprocity then places it in exactly the one even or two odd blocks claimed, since a degree-N component forces i+B+C=N. This also covers N=0 and guards against missing multiplicities. A separately rebuilt beta Gram/generalized-eigenvalue calculation through N=8 matched the block spectra (maximum discrepancy 1.39e−12), the minima, and the parity counts.
residual_risks: The finite spectral calculation is numerical; the exact all-N conclusion uses the independent polynomial and path argument above.
